That same file also lists a 2026-10-28 close of 2357.62, which matches the verified series, so the conflict is isolated to the latest close. Indicator values line up: 10 EMA 2355.12, 50 SMA 2529.98, 200 SMA 2159.18, RSI 31.69, MACD −62.30, signal −53.08, histogram −9.22, ATR 86.97. Bollinger values come only from the snapshot (middle 2406.56, upper 2541.38, lower 2271.74). VWMA is not in the snapshot; the indicator tool prints 2382.05 on 2026-10-29 and is used only as a volume-weighted trend check.

## Indicator set

Eight complementary indicators were used, chosen for a market that just broke a multi-week range after a large September rally and an October unwind:

- **close_10_ema** — short-term momentum and tactical trend.
- **close_50_sma** — medium-term trend and the overhead level that has contained rallies since early October.
- **close_200_sma** — long-term benchmark; still rising, so the strategic tape is not the same as the short-term tape.
- **macd** and **macdh** — momentum direction and whether the downside impulse is still expanding. The signal line is taken from the verified snapshot rather than a separate series, to avoid a redundant third MACD print.
- **rsi** — oversold/divergence filter. In a downtrend, sub-30 is a warning, not an automatic buy.
- **atr** — volatility for stop distance and size. Bollinger bands from the snapshot supply the range context without another indicator call.
- **vwma** — volume-weighted confirmation that the latest decline is not just thin-print noise.

## Regime

ETH-USD is in a **short- and medium-term downtrend inside a still-intact long-term uptrend**. Price is below the 10 EMA and the 50 SMA, but it remains above the rising 200 SMA. That split matters: tactical traders are fighting a declining 50-day average, while strategic holders still have a higher long-term average underneath.

The path into this setup is visible in the closes. After the June 2026 washout (close 1506.51 low area on 2026-06-06, close 1580.86), price rebuilt through July and then exploded on 2026-08-19 (close 2251.46, volume 29.6 billion) and 2026-08-21 (close 2515.28). September extended that move to a verified recent high close of 2776.47 on 2026-09-21, with an intraday high of 2805.50 that day in the raw file. From 2026-09-22 through 2026-10-06, closes clustered roughly 2668–2727. The break started 2026-10-07 (close 2573.53, volume 20.1 billion) and 2026-10-08 (close 2471.91, low 2406.15). October never reclaimed the early-month shelf. The verified 30-day sequence ends with 2320.28 (10-26), 2347.73 (10-27), 2357.62 (10-28), and **2263.38 (10-29)**.

On 2026-10-29 the session itself was a range expansion lower: open 2357.33, high 2371.85, low 2252.86, close 2263.38, volume 13.06 billion. That volume is above the quiet mid-October prints (for example 5.56 billion on 2026-10-10 and 6.09 billion on 2026-10-25) and is the heaviest day since 2026-10-08. The close finished near the session low, so this was not a quiet drift under the averages.

## Trend structure

**Short term is decisively negative.** The 10 EMA has fallen every session from 2670.56 on 2026-10-07 to 2355.12 on 2026-10-29. Price closed about 92 points under that average on the verified close. A first tactical repair would be a daily close back above the 10 EMA, not a wick through it. Until that happens, bounces into 2355–2385 are rallies into a declining average, not trend reversals.

**Medium term is the binding constraint.** The 50 SMA peaked near 2556 in mid-October and has been slipping: 2546.59 on 2026-10-07, 2529.98 on 2026-10-29. Price is roughly 267 points, or about 10.5% of the current price, below it. That gap is large enough that mean-reversion longs are trading against the intermediate trend, not with it. The 50 SMA and the Bollinger upper band (2541.38) now sit in the same neighborhood, so 2530–2541 is a stacked resistance zone if any squeeze develops. It is not nearby support.

**Long term is still constructive, with a caveat.** The 200 SMA bottomed near 2003 in mid-August and has risen steadily to 2159.18. Verified close 2263.38 is still about 104 points above it. That is the bull case: the October selloff has not yet violated the long-term average that caught the post-June recovery. The caveat is distance. In late August and September, price was hundreds of points above the 200 SMA. The cushion has compressed. A daily close through 2159 would change the regime from “pullback in an uptrend” to “long-term trend damage.” That level should be treated as a strategic line, not as a guaranteed bounce.

**Volume agrees with the decline.** VWMA on 2026-10-29 is 2382.05, above both the close and the 10 EMA, and it has been falling since early October (2694.64 on 2026-10-06, 2662.29 on 2026-10-08, 2382.05 now). When a volume-weighted average sits above price and is itself declining, recent heavier volume has been associated with lower prices, not with accumulation at the highs. The August spike was the opposite pattern: VWMA was below price while price and volume expanded together.

## Momentum

MACD confirms the trend break and says the impulse is not finished. The line was strongly positive through the September advance (peak area near +169 on 2026-08-27, still +97 on 2026-09-22, +59.94 on 2026-10-06). It crossed below zero between 2026-10-10 (+3.23) and 2026-10-11 (−2.07) and has trended to **−62.30**, the most negative reading in this 120-day window aside from the early-July print of −71.63. The verified signal is −53.08, so MACD remains below its signal. The histogram is −9.22, negative for 22 consecutive sessions since 2026-10-08, but less negative than the −35.93 trough on 2026-10-12 and the −21.62 reading on 2026-10-19. That is deceleration of the histogram, not a bullish crossover. On 2026-10-28 the histogram improved to −5.99 as price bounced to 2357.62; 2026-10-29 pushed it back to −9.22. Momentum tried to stabilize and failed on the latest bar.

RSI tells the same story with a different clock. It was overbought on the August spike (88.30 on 2026-08-21, 72.18 on 2026-09-21) and neutral-to-firm in the 2668–2727 shelf (59.7–64.0 from 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-06). It has since lived in the 30s for most of the second half of October, with only a brief lift to 45.94 on 2026-10-21. The verified reading is **31.69**, just above the conventional 30 oversold line, and it is the lowest print since 2026-07-01 (39.74 was the early-July low in this window; the June crash is outside the RSI lookback returned here). Two practical points follow. First, 31.7 is stretched enough that chasing fresh shorts at the low of a wide down day is a poor risk/reward. Second, it is not yet a reversal signal. RSI spent time in the mid-30s from 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-20 and price still made lower closes. In a trend, oversold can stay oversold. A constructive divergence would require price to undercut 2252.86 or 2263.38 while RSI holds above 31.69. That has not happened; the latest low in price and the latest low in RSI arrived together.

## Volatility and location in the range

ATR is **86.97**, down from the mid-90s in late September (103.59 on 2026-09-23) and from 94.36 on 2026-10-22, but up from the mid-40s that prevailed in the August base before the breakout. Volatility has cooled from the September expansion, yet a one-ATR move is still about 3.8% of the 2263 close. That is the right unit for stops. A stop inside 40–50 points is inside noise. A 1.0–1.5 ATR stop is roughly 87–130 points.

Bollinger bands frame where the 2026-10-29 close sits. Middle band 2406.56 is a 20-day average and the first mean-reversion magnet. Upper band 2541.38 aligns with the 50 SMA. Lower band 2271.74 was marginally violated by the verified close of 2263.38, and the session low of 2252.86 is clearly through it. A close through the lower band after a multi-week decline is a momentum event, not by itself a buy. In strong trends price can ride the lower band. What would change the interpretation is a close back inside the band, ideally back above 2272 and then toward 2407, with RSI turning up from the low 30s and the histogram shrinking toward zero. None of those confirmations are in hand on this bar.

The recent price map, using only tool-printed levels, is:

- **2252.86** — 2026-10-29 session low. Nearest intraday reference under the close.
- **2263.38** — verified close, just under the lower Bollinger band.
- **2271.74** — lower band. Immediate reclaim level.
- **2320–2358** — the 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-28 close cluster that just failed.
- **2355.12** — 10 EMA. First trend-repair line.
- **2382–2407** — VWMA and Bollinger middle. Zone where a bounce stops being a reflex and starts testing supply.
- **2444–2471** — failed rebound closes from 2026-10-12, 2026-10-20, and 2026-10-21.
- **2529.98 / 2541.38** — 50 SMA and upper band. Medium-term trend gate.
- **2159.18** — 200 SMA. Strategic trend line, about one ATR-plus below the close.

I am not calling 2253 or 2159 “validated support” from prior bounces. The tools show they are today’s low and today’s long average. They are reference levels, not proven floors.

## Trade implications

**For existing long exposure.** The intermediate trend is against the position. The 2026-10-07/08 break of the 2668–2727 shelf, the MACD zero cross, and the failure of the 2320–2358 cluster are enough to reduce risk rather than average down into a falling 10 EMA. If the position is strategic and sized for the 200 SMA, the line in the sand is a daily close under 2159, not a tag of 2253. If the position is tactical, the invalidation is already active: price is under the 10 EMA and the 50 SMA, and the latest bar closed near its low on rising volume. A practical hedge or trim trigger is a failure to reclaim 2272–2320 within the next one to two sessions. Holding full size while hoping RSI “is oversold” fights the indicator’s own warning that extremes persist in trends.

**For new longs.** Do not buy the lower-band tag as a standalone signal. The higher-probability long is a two-step reclaim, not a knife catch. Step one is a daily close back above 2272 and then above the broken 2320–2358 cluster, with RSI turning up from 31.69 rather than making a lower low. Step two, for anything larger than a tactical bounce, is a close above the 10 EMA (2355) and a MACD histogram cross back toward zero. Until the 50 SMA near 2530 is regained, any long is a countertrend trade and should be sized that way. ATR of 87 argues for smaller size than was appropriate in the August base, when ATR was in the mid-40s. A stop for a tactical long, if one is taken only after a reclaim, belongs beyond 2252.86 by a fraction of ATR, not a few dollars under the entry. If 2252.86 breaks on a close and RSI prints a fresh low, the long thesis is wrong and the 200 SMA at 2159 becomes the next major reference, roughly 104 points lower.

**For shorts.** The trend, the MACD position under its signal, and the volume-weighted average above price all support the bearish bias. The problem is location. Shorting 2263 after a 94-point intraday range (high 2371.85 to low 2252.86) and with RSI at 31.69 is late. Better short locations are failed bounces into supply: first the 10 EMA / prior cluster at 2355–2385, then VWMA and the Bollinger middle at 2382–2407, and only later 2444–2471. A short initiated into those zones can use a stop above the zone plus a fraction of ATR, because a close back above 2407 would mean price has re-entered the 20-day mean and the immediate breakdown is failing. Covering into 2253–2272 is reasonable for tactical shorts; pressing for 2159 is a separate, wider trade that should not use the same stop. If price reclaims 2355 on a closing basis and the histogram continues to contract, the short edge from this leg is decaying even if the 50 SMA is still overhead.

**What would actually change the call.** A bullish regime shift needs more than one green day. The minimum sequence is: close back inside the Bollinger bands, RSI divergence or at least a higher low versus 31.69, histogram crossing back above zero, and price above the 10 EMA. A bearish regime shift, from pullback to long-term damage, is a daily close under the 200 SMA at 2159 with ATR expanding back through the mid-90s. Between those two outcomes, the base case is a volatile decline or chop under 2407, with 2253 and 2159 as the downside references and 2355 then 2530 as the upside gates.

This is a market-structure read of ETH-USD as of 2026-10-29, not a prediction of the next session and not investment advice. Crypto can gap through ATR-based levels; size should assume the 87-point ATR is a floor for noise, not a ceiling.

StockTwits is only 17 on-topic messages, all clustered in about 45 minutes on 2026-10-29. Reddit is five relevant posts with no vote or comment counts. X is the only substantive multi-day sample (130 posts fetched; a retrieval model selected the set below, so it is a sample, not a census).

ETH-USD is treated as a crypto asset (Ethereum USD, CCC). No company fundamentals are assumed. Cashtags in the raw feeds (`$ETH.X`, `$ETH`) are mapped to **ETH-USD** only. Related tickers mentioned by users (for example BMNR / BitMine) are context for ETH-USD flows, not the subject of this report.

No configured vendor served headlines for ETH-USD. Institutional news framing cannot be scored. Nothing below is inferred from “missing news.” Macro items (Fed hold, inflation, oil, geopolitics) appear only as claims inside X posts, not as verified wire copy.

#### StockTwits — bearish retail tags, one-hour snapshot, small n

Screened sample: **17** on-topic messages (of 30 fetched). User-applied tags: **Bullish 2 (12%)**, **Bearish 8 (47%)**, **Unlabeled 7**. Among the 10 labeled messages the split is **2 bullish / 8 bearish (20/80)** — a clear bearish lean, not a 50/50 coin-flip and nowhere near a 70/30 bullish crowd. Base the ratio on counts, not the 12% figure alone: eight bearish tags versus two bullish tags in a 17-message set.

A separate classifier read of all 17 on-topic posts (labeled or not): **3 bullish, 5 bearish, 4 neutral, 5 unclear**. Directional calls still lean bearish (3 vs 5), but a large neutral/unclear share means the tag ratio overstates how uniformly negative the text is. Several unlabeled posts are dip-management or level-calling rather than pure panic.

All 17 timestamps fall on **2026-10-29 between 20:09Z and 20:53Z**. This is an end-of-window burst, not a seven-day retail series. Do not treat 80% bearish labels as the week’s base rate.
